biography: Noah Harris, born in Seoul, South Korea, discovered his passion for racing through late-night viewings of Formula One with his grandfather. Initially drawn to the technical aspects of the cars, Noah's interest quickly shifted to the drivers and the sheer audacity of their maneuvers. His first experience behind the wheel came at a local karting track on his 12th birthday, an event that solidified his ambition. Lacking substantial financial backing, Noah has navigated his early career through grit and determination, relying on sponsorships from local businesses and support from his family. A defining moment came during the Korean National Karting Championship where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to a podium finish, demonstrating his relentless spirit and exceptional overtaking skills. Currently, Noah is competing as an independent driver in the Formula Regional Asian Championship, aiming to prove his mettle and secure a coveted spot in a higher racing tier.
drivingStyle: Noah's driving style is characterized by a calculated, defensive approach. He prioritizes consistency and tire management over outright aggression, often sacrificing a few positions early in a race to maintain a strong pace towards the end. He's particularly adept at reading the track and identifying optimal braking points, allowing him to conserve energy and capitalize on opponents' mistakes. While not the flashiest driver, Noah's tactical awareness and ability to withstand pressure make him a formidable competitor, especially in longer races.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks he got from his grandmother during race weekends.
Listens to classical music, specifically Mozart, before every race to calm his nerves.
Has a meticulous pre-race checklist that he reviews three times before getting into the car.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about how fast you can go for one lap; it's about how consistently you can push the limits without crossing them. It's a war of attrition.
careerHighlight: Winning the Korean National Karting Championship in 2021, despite starting from the back of the grid, proving his ability to overcome adversity and showcasing his raw talent to the racing community.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Macau Grand Prix Formula Regional race due to a sudden downpour, costing him a potential victory and valuable championship points.
